audience.programmeDescription: Tilburg’s Dutch Psychology track studies mind and behaviour through broad psychological foundations, research and professional skills. Students then complete a major and a thesis. This example uses Work and Organizational Psychology, whose major courses are taught in English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers broad psychology with organisational and leadership study, and related priorities in clinical health and lifespan development or brain, cognition and data methods. Tilburg provides a dedicated psychology major, professional training and thesis. Academic overlap does not establish clinical registration or postgraduate admission.

componentNotes.y1-skills-b: Academic Skills B requires passing Academic Skills A. The first-year sequence completes A before B.
componentNotes.y1-skills-c: Academic Skills C includes information-literacy and plagiarism tests and 20 experimental-subject participation hours. These are part of the first year that must be completed before thesis entry. GROW guidance carries no credit.
componentNotes.y2-work: This example uses the Work and Organizational Psychology major. Work Psychology, Organizational Psychology and Diversity and Inclusion at Work each carry 6 EC and are taught in English, even within the Dutch track.
componentNotes.y3-applied-work: Applied Work and Organizational Psychology is the 6 EC third-year major course. It applies the PATHS model to an organisational problem with stakeholder feedback, a group presentation, individual logs and required participation.
componentNotes.y3-mobility: The 30 EC choice space can contain a minor or electives, including study abroad. At least 12 EC must come from non-selected psychology majors or predefined psychology electives. An alternative to this rule requires prior Examination Board approval. No particular choice is assumed.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Thesis entry requires all first-year courses and at least 60 EC from later years. The February group is advised to have 138 EC. A quantitative thesis is illustrated; qualitative or systematic-review versions require their corresponding 3 EC elective before submission.

Applied Work and Organizational Psychology is the 6 EC third-year major course. It applies the PATHS model to an organisational problem with stakeholder feedback, a group presentation, individual logs and required participation.

The 30 EC choice space can contain a minor or electives, including study abroad. At least 12 EC must come from non-selected psychology majors or predefined psychology electives. An alternative to this rule requires prior Examination Board approval. No particular choice is assumed.

Thesis entry requires all first-year courses and at least 60 EC from later years. The February group is advised to have 138 EC. A quantitative thesis is illustrated; qualitative or systematic-review versions require their corresponding 3 EC elective before submission.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD111.name: Personal Leadership
BENLEAD111.text: Introduces self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Students use personality and emotional-intelligence profiles to reflect on group dynamics, study leadership cases, and develop a personal plan with practical goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection, with attention to differences in their scientific support.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.text: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

DISDATA212.text: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

GOSPHIL212.text: Ethics examines moral reasoning through historical and contemporary theories and close philosophical reading. Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. Reflection and research essays develop interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

HCBCOGN112.text: Neurobiology studies nervous systems and behaviour through comparative anatomy, evolution and physiology. An attentional-blink experiment and a team research proposal develop engagement with empirical research, experimental design and ethical reflection.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
